g.text: LLD 2 / 3 — STATES, RETRIES + GITHUB PROOF
Each check attempt has its own ID. A stale worker cannot finish a newer attempt.
TASK STATE TRANSITIONS
Authority is checked against active membership in this
task’s room.
OPEN → IN_PROGRESS
Task owner or room lead starts work.
OPEN / IN_PROGRESS → BLOCKED
Task owner or room lead records a blocker.
BLOCKED → IN_PROGRESS
Task owner or room lead explicitly confirms it is
resolved.
IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETE
Verifier only, in the proof commit transaction.
COMPLETE → no direct change. Correct with an authorized
compensating audit event.
TASK PROOF STATUS
AWAITING_PROOF → VERIFYING
Authorized owner, delegate, or room lead submits a PR.
Create a new attempt.
PENDING_RETRY → VERIFYING
Retry trigger creates a new attempt ID.
VERIFYING → VERIFIED
Only the successful completion transaction.
VERIFYING → PENDING_RETRY
Transient GitHub failure, changed SHA/check, stale
task/policy, or CAS conflict. Task remains open.
VERIFYING → REJECTED
Permanent proof failure. Corrected submission or policy
change is required to try again.
ATTEMPT STATUS + OWNERSHIP
Each attempt has UUID, attempt number, captured task
version, policy revision/hash, PR URL, state, retry
time, and result.
CHECKING → RETRY_LATER
Verifier records transient failure.
CHECKING → REJECTED
Verifier records permanent proof failure.
CHECKING → VERIFIED
Repository completion transaction only.
Old attempt → SUPERSEDED
When a newer attempt starts or its task/policy snapshot
is stale. Every update requires task.active_attempt_id
= this attempt ID. A late worker then changes nothing.
COMPLETION CAS — EXACT GUARD
One short BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; no network calls inside it.
UPDATE tasks … WHERE task_id = :task
AND version = :captured_task_version
AND status = 'IN_PROGRESS'
AND proof_status = 'VERIFYING'
AND active_attempt_id = :attempt_id
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM policy_heads
WHERE policy_id = :policy_id
AND current_revision = :revision
AND current_hash = :hash);
Also require the attempt row still be CHECKING with the same attempt ID. Zero updated task rows =
conflict: rollback every write, reload and reauthorize/reverify. Same transaction updates task +
attempt, inserts proof snapshot + audit event + outbox, and marks inbox DONE.
WHAT INCREMENTS TASK VERSION?
Every persisted task change: status, proof status, active attempt, owner, delegate set, allowed paths,
dependencies, blocker state/text, policy link, title, deadline, or other task field. Every mutation
inserts one audit event for the resulting version; UNIQUE(task_id, task_version) enforces one event per
version. Policy edits use immutable revisions and a current-revision pointer. The final CAS checks both
revision and hash, even when the task itself did not change.
TRANSITION + FAILURE TABLE
Trigger → durable result
Authorized PR submitted → attempt CHECKING; task proof VERIFYING; task stays IN_PROGRESS.
All checks pass; task + policy CAS succeeds → task COMPLETE / proof VERIFIED / attempt VERIFIED; proof + audit + outbox + inbox result commit
together.
GitHub timeout, 429, 5xx, network error → attempt RETRY_LATER; task proof PENDING_RETRY; task stays open; retry with bounded backoff.
Required check missing or pending → RETRY_LATER; retry after check webhook or scheduled poll.
New check rerun or changed final read → old attempt SUPERSEDED; task stays open; new verification attempt.
Permanent repo/author/path/diff/check failure → attempt REJECTED; task stays open; only corrected PR or policy change allows a new attempt.
Task/policy CAS conflict → rollback all completion writes; reload current task/policy and reauthorize; create a new attempt if still eligible.
BLOCKED task → no proof completion; owner/lead must first move it to IN_PROGRESS.
Duplicate event → return stored inbox result; never run the task command twice.
Worker crash → expired inbox/outbox lease can be reclaimed. Remote post succeeded but ack was lost → possible duplicate reply; task completion still
occurs once.
REQUIRED CHECK SELECTION
Policy entry: exact check name + optional GitHub App ID (+ workflow ID when same key could come from
multiple workflows). Missing App ID means any App; if that creates ambiguous publishers, reject policy
config until pinned.
For each required key:
1. Read every page of check runs for the exact PR head SHA.
2. Match exact name and configured App ID.
3. Pick newest execution by this stable order:
Actions: highest run_attempt, then run_started_at, then run_id.
Other checks: check-suite created_at, then check-run started_at; check_run ID breaks an exact tie.
4. No matching run or no ordering timestamp → RETRY_LATER (fail closed).
5. Pass only when selected SHA matches, status=completed, conclusion=success.
6. A newer pending run replaces an older success; pending is never success.
SECOND READ + ACCEPTED RACE
After first validation, re-read PR head and each selected check. Compare a fingerprint per required
key:
(check name, App ID, head SHA, check_run ID, check_suite ID, status, conclusion, started_at,
completed_at).
For Actions also compare (workflow/run ID, run_attempt, run_started_at, updated_at).
Any field change, new selected ID/attempt, or new pending rerun invalidates this attempt. Restart
against current data. The five-second freshness window begins at the final GitHub response and ends
when the SQLite transaction starts.
Accepted race: GitHub can update after that final read but before SQLite commits. A later run does not
rewrite the proof; it records the exact SHA and run/check IDs that were read. A post-commit rerun
webhook appends an alert event but does not silently reopen the task.
